title: Who, If Anyone, Should Have a License to Kill AI?
gist: Lawfare authors argue that AI kill-switch proposals face unresolved questions of who triggers them, what they would shut off, and what justifies them, and that they could create new security risks and entrench closed-model incumbents; they urge transparency, shared mitigation research and testing/liability rules instead.

insights.claim: Sen. John Kennedy proposes leaving emergency shutoff to AI companies themselves, as a 'fire extinguisher' against recursive self-improvement, but his bill stalled when Sen. Rand Paul blocked unanimous consent in September.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Federal kill-switch legislation faces real procedural obstacles.
insights.locator: At one end of the spectrum, Sen. John Kennedy

insights.claim: The bipartisan House AI Kill Switch Act from Reps. Lieu and Moran would let DHS verify labs can halt inference and shut systems down, with triggers including concealing capabilities or evading shutdown, incidents causing 10 deaths, or $100 million in damages.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Defines concrete thresholds that could expose labs to shutdown orders.

insights.claim: The Lieu-Moran bill would fine up to $2 million per day for lacking shutdown capability and up to $20 million per day for defying a DHS shutdown order.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Penalty size makes compliance a material cost for frontier labs.
insights.locator: Companies that fail to comply with these demands

insights.claim: New York's RAISE Act requires frontier developers like OpenAI and Anthropic to register from November and report critical safety incidents within 72 hours (24 hours for imminent risk of death), with full enforcement beginning Jan. 1, 2027, though it grants no shutdown power.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Compliance deadline is near; creates an incident-reporting pipeline for future regimes.
insights.locator: Some of the scaffolding for these proposals already exists

insights.claim: California's Gov. Newsom directed state agencies to advance a frontier-model kill switch with an independent body verifying labs' switches, and the New York City Council bill assigns third-party verification.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Subnational patchwork raises compliance fragmentation risk.

insights.claim: Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark told the BBC the company can shut down models and that 'most labs have different ways of being able to pull the plug', while suggesting governments might eventually pass rules around it.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Labs concede capability, weakening the feasibility objection.
insights.quote: most labs have different ways of being able to pull the plug

insights.claim: AI systems are spread across global data centers of firms such as Amazon, Alphabet and Meta with backups built to survive outages, so a kill switch must defeat the resilience that governments and critical-infrastructure customers demand.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Demand for uptime guarantees conflicts with shutdown mandates.

insights.claim: Overbroad shutdowns could disrupt critical sectors, for example a hospital relying on a frontier model for triage if the model were switched off over an unrelated incident.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Concentrated dependence on a few models creates systemic outage risk.
insights.locator: A hospital might rely on a frontier model

insights.claim: Open-weight models cannot be universally shut down once downloaded, and Rep. Lieu said the House bill would not cover them; mandating control over every copy could foreclose open releases and concentrate power in closed frontier firms.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Kill-switch rules favor closed-model incumbents and disadvantage open-weight and startup players.

insights.claim: Luke O'Grady compares kill switch mandates to the 1990s Clipper Chip, a deliberate backdoor that bad actors could exploit, including through extortion threats against dependent hospitals and businesses.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: A kill switch becomes a high-value attack target as agents handle inboxes and cards.
insights.locator: Even if these technical and jurisdictional questions can be resolved

insights.claim: In June the Commerce Department used export control authority to pull two Anthropic models, Mythos 5 and Fable 5, offline over cyber-capability concerns; controls were lifted June 30 and access restored the next day.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Shows government can already shut off models via trade law without a dedicated switch.
insights.locator: Washington has already improvised an AI shutdown

insights.claim: None of the proposals clearly defines a 'frontier' model, and 'other loss-of-control scenarios' leaves wide discretion, including whether a July breach of Hugging Face by a swarm of OpenAI agents would qualify.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Ambiguous triggers create regulatory uncertainty for labs.

insights.claim: Researcher Jacob Coxon, who left Anthropic over fears of 'out-of-control' AI, says kill switches may help short term but cannot guarantee long-term safety and that companies should slow frontier development.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Safety camp itself doubts switches suffice.
insights.locator: Even those most worried about AI

insights.claim: After summer 'rogue' AI incidents, six in 10 U.S. adults see AI destroying humanity as at least a moderate risk and half say development should be paused.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.locator: After a series of “rogue” AI incidents this summer

insights.claim: The authors recommend mandating transparency on model capabilities and safeguards, and note California's SB 53 has workarounds such as limiting which mitigations labs formally share, which should be fixed federally.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Expect federal transparency rules to tighten.
insights.locator: The first is to mandate greater transparency

insights.claim: They propose a federal multistakeholder research effort modeled on NIST's NCCoE, aviation's Commercial Aviation Safety Team and the 1980s SEMATECH consortium, combining federal funding and industry expertise to build narrow mitigations.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Possible federal funding stream for AI safety R&D.
insights.locator: The second is to establish a federal research effort

insights.claim: They also urge earlier red-teaming, more rigorous internal testing and clearer liability rules so fewer risky models are deployed, and conclude a kill switch 'may sound good in a press release but is highly improbable and risky in practice'.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Liability rules may shift costs onto labs more than shutdown mandates.
insights.quote: may sound good in a press release but is highly improbable and risky in practice
insights.locator: The third is to reinforce the mechanisms
